# Sundhedsklyngerne

**Sundhedsklyngerne** (the health clusters) are 21 geographical regional collaboration units within the Danish healthcare system [^src1]. They represent a structural paradigm shift in clinical quality reporting, moving away from a strictly hospital-centered model toward a comprehensive, population-based approach [^src1]. 

In the context of the 2024 annual report on [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark), prepared by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), Sundhedsklyngerne serve as the primary geographical units for reporting quality results [^src1]. By organizing data around the patients' residence in these 21 clusters, the system mandates that all healthcare sectors—specifically general practice, hospitals, and practicing cardiologists—collaborate on a shared population responsibility for atrial fibrillation patients [^src1]. Going forward, the database's results are primarily reported with a starting point in these 21 health clusters rather than isolated hospital departments, supporting an integrated healthcare strategy with shared cross-sectoral responsibility [^src1].
